title: Land in the Earth System 2 - Course information
Land in the Earth System 2 - Course information
text:
Course description
This course is a lecture, taught at the University of Bern in the Masters program for Geography and for Climate Sciences students. It follows the online textbook Land in the Earth System.
The course advances the introduction of fundamental processes governing terrestrial biosphere functioning. Standard and simple demonstration models will be introduced and applied for demonstrating terrestrial carbon cycle functioning and and Earth system dynamics. The course builds on Land in the Earth System 1 and deepens its scope, while covering largely the same thematic ground - from the global carbon cycle, land-climate interactions, ecohydrology, to Earth system dynamics. In addition, scientific methods, data, and research challenges will be discussed.
The course is organised into a mix of lectures, self-study, and student presentations. Lecture notes containing all relevant content will be made available. No podcasts will be recorded.

title: Land in the Earth System 2 - Course information
text:
Learning objectives

Identify the controls on water, carbon, and nutrient dynamics across the Earth.
Describe Earth system research challenges related to the terrestrial biosphere.
Predict responses of terrestrial ecosystem processes environmental change based on conceptual, empirical, and mathematical models.

title: Land in the Earth System 2 - Course information
text:
Target audience and prerequisites
Master students in Geography and Climate Science. Contents of Land in the Earth System 1 (LES 1) are the basis. Students that did not take LES 1 are expected to learn its contents through self-study prior to the start of LES 2 using the online textbook Land in the Earth System.

The lead for this course is by by Prof. Benjamin Stocker and co-taught with Dr. Fabian Bernhard and Dr. Fabrice Lacroix. The website is a product of the group for Geocomputation and Earth Observation, Institute of Geography, University of Bern.

title: 1  Logistics
text:
Lead: Prof. Benjamin Stocker; contributing lecturers: Dr. Fabian Bernhard and Dr. Fabrice Lacroix.
Course language is English.
Monday 14.15-16.00 is our presence time, use it for your communication with us.
The course is mix of lectures and poster presentations by students.
Contents are partly covered by the lecture notes Land in the Earth System, Part II.
The contents of the lecture notes are covered by the written exam. From experience, personal presence and an active engagement in the lectures is strongly associated with success in the written exam.
In groups of two, students create and present a poster (printed in A1) that describes a published peer-reviewed scientific research article (not a review or opinion article) as if they were the authors of it. Posters should be created following recommendations for scientific posters (see Section 3.1).
Articles are proposed by the lecturers (see Section 3.2) or may be suggested by the students.
The posters are graded together with the written exam (each 50%).
The exam is in written form, closed book, and takes place in the last session during the semester.

title: 1  Logistics
text:
1.2 Use of AI
The use of AI services for text creation should be considered with caution. You are solely responsible for the content of any output that graded as part of this course. Accurate descriptions of scientific methods and results, justified interpretations, and the correct referencing of original sources is mandatory and is often unreliably solved by AI. Full control over outputs by the human author is undespensable. Consider the view of the lecturer on this topic, see here.
